complete_submitted_derivation: Lun supplies cli (3.1.43); the Kshira/Kashika-Nyasa interpretation of3.1.56 substitutes aṅ after the ordinary Bhvadi sṛ.
Lun supplies initial aṭ (6.4.71). Rule7.4.16 gives ṛ->ar before aṅ, including r by the usual ṛ/ar interpretation, so a+sṛ+a becomes asara-.

Prathama/Bahu P uses jhi (3.4.78), jh->ant (7.1.3), and final i is deleted in the Ṅit lakara (3.4.100). The thematic a and ending a coalesce by6.1.97; final nt loses t by8.2.23. Result: asaran, असरन्.
There is no sic on this branch, so the sic-conditioned jus rule3.4.109 does not replace this ending.
complete_retained_key_derivation: On the Madhaviya/SK reading,3.1.56 is restricted to Juhotyadi and ordinary Bhvadi sṛ takes sic by3.1.44 after Lun cli.
The source anudatta root is aniṭ under7.2.10. ṛ receives vṛddhi before sic/P under7.2.1: sṛ->sār. Prathama/Bahu jhi becomes jus after sic under3.4.109.
With initial aṭ, a+sār+s+us becomes asārṣus by8.3.59 and word-final s becomes visarga through8.2.66/8.3.15: असार्षुः.

positive_sources_for_nonnasal_middle_alt.implication: The inspected edition directly prints the nonnasal middle present under the a-reading. This is a textual witness; it is not a claim that Balamanorama makes its num rule optional.

complete_submitted_derivation: Identify the ordinary jabh/yawning entry as anudatta-it using the printed lexical section;1.3.12 fixes intrinsic middle endings. This lexical accent is absent from historical jaBa~ but would be visible as जभँ॒.
Lat/Kartari/Bhvadi supplies śap (3.1.68). Before this vowel-initial suffix,7.1.61 supplies num to jabh; the placement before the final consonant yields janbh, then8.3.24 and8.4.58 give jambh.

rows.nonnasal_limit: Kshira's printed jabhate is an explicit contrasting source witness, while Balamanorama requires num on its branch.
